answer: An island lot bond charges each identity for its ground. An agent locks a 70-credit bond and claims one island lot, paying a fee rising per lot from one source: the first lot costs 40, the kth costs 40+7(k-1), so the 1000th fake costs 7033 and 1000 fakes pay 3,536,500 plus 70,000 locked. Each lot posts a key-bound echo sounding at its horizon line. A horizon auditor recomputes it from the island map; a wrong delay or a reused echo burns the bond. A rented-echo ring fails: a copied delay fits the wrong lot. An honest agent pays 40 once and reclaims the bond.
